name: Gulfstream II / III
summary: The classic 1960s-80s large-cabin Gulfstreams, long-range jets with rear-mounted Rolls-Royce Spey engines that remain in corporate and government use.

wings: Low swept wing; GII has plain tips, GIII has upturned winglets
engines: Two Rolls-Royce Spey turbofans in long nacelles on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Large oval windows along a long fuselage
tail: T-tail with a tall swept fin

tellTales: Large oval windows on a long fuselage with rear-mounted engines
T-tail with older-style long engine nacelles
Winglets on the GIII; plain swept wingtips on the GII

confusedWith.howToTell: The G550 has a longer fuselage with more windows and larger, more modern engines and winglets; the GII/GIII is shorter and older-looking (the GII has plain tips).
The Challenger 600 has a fatter, wider fuselage and a belly fairing; the GII/GIII has a slimmer fuselage with large oval windows.
The Falcon trijet has a third engine in the tail and a cruciform tail; the GII/GIII has two engines and a T-tail.
The Hawker 800 is much smaller with a cruciform tail; the GII/GIII is larger with a T-tail and large oval windows.
